role: Repair close-out reviewer in a water utility's distribution network team, checking each completed leak repair job record before it is signed off
setting: A regional water utility logs every water main leak repair as a structured job record assembled from the field crew's handheld, the network control room's valve log, the laboratory sample system and the highways reinstatement tracker. Before a job can be closed, a reviewer must make five decisions about it. Is third-party damage supported? What close-out action is needed? What should the asset team do next for the main? How long was supply interrupted? How far has the site been reinstated? Records arrive one at a time. No section carries free-text notes, so every judgement rests on comparing coded fields, times, sizes, lists and flags across sections.

third_party_cause.instructions: The leak was caused by third-party damage to the main.

criteria.true: Strike marks or puncture, with works active before report.
criteria.false: No physical evidence, or works only after report.

closeout_action.instructions: What should happen to this repair job at close-out review?

criteria.close: Tests, samples and reinstatement all complete and mutually consistent.
criteria.close_with_actions: Safety checks confirmed; only reinstatement or record tidying outstanding.
criteria.hold: One test, sample or approval result still needs confirming.
criteria.reopen: Failed test, unapproved fitting or quality fault requires revisit.

asset_followup.instructions: What follow-up should the asset team plan for this main?

criteria.none: Isolated or external failure; no asset work beyond repair.
criteria.monitor: Deploy acoustic loggers and review the main after a quarter.
criteria.condition_survey: Commission an excavated condition survey of the affected section.
criteria.expedite_replacement: Bring the main's replacement forward in the capital programme.

interruption_duration.instructions: How long were customers without supply during the repair?
criteria: No properties lost supply at any point
Supply off for more than 12 hours

reinstatement_stage.instructions: How far has the excavation site been reinstated?
criteria: Open: excavation still open or only fenced off
Temporary: backfilled with temporary surface, no permanent layer
Permanent: permanent surface laid, inspection not yet logged
Signed_off: permanent surface laid and inspection logged as passed

factors.name: fitting_size_mismatch
factors.description: Gap between the main's nominal diameter in the asset section and the size range of the repair fitting recorded in the repair section; trivial cases are unit rounding (inches vs mm) inside tolerance, major cases are a fitting range that excludes the main's outside diameter

factors.name: substitution_approved
factors.description: Whether an approved material or fitting substitution reference with an approver code exists for the repair, which legitimises a fitting or material that differs from the asset record

factors.name: pressure_test_outcome
factors.description: Sequence of post-repair pressure test results logged against the job

factors.name: water_quality_state
factors.description: Post-repair chlorine residual and bacteriological sample position: clear, low residual followed by flushing and a passing resample, low residual with no resample, or sample taken but result pending

factors.name: interruption_hours
factors.description: True supply interruption length from the first isolation valve shut to the last valve reopened affecting customers; zero when the repair was done under pressure or with full rezoning; values cluster near the 3 and 12 hour boundaries in a share of records

factors.name: estimate_drift
factors.description: How far the planned interruption estimate in the job section departs from the actual valve times; a decoy that is sometimes small and sometimes crosses a scale boundary

factors.name: reinstatement_state
factors.description: Actual reinstatement progress shown by the layer records and inspection list

factors.name: failure_cause
factors.description: True underlying cause of the leak, shown only through fracture type, strike marks, pipe wall condition and ground readings in the findings section

factors.name: third_party_permit_timing
factors.description: Whether street works permits within 50 m exist and whether their start date falls before or after the leak was first reported; post-report permits are decoys

factors.name: strike_marks_ambiguous
factors.description: Strike mark evidence is recorded as 'possible' rather than yes or no, or a puncture fracture sits on a heavily pitted pipe wall, leaving third-party cause contestable

factors.name: prior_bursts_5y
factors.description: Number of earlier bursts logged on the same main ID in the five years before this report

factors.name: replacement_scheduled
factors.description: Whether the main already sits in the capital replacement programme with a planned year, which lowers the need for new asset follow-up despite a poor burst history

factors.name: prior_external_share
factors.description: Proportion of prior bursts coded as third-party damage rather than structural failure; a high share mitigates an alarming burst count

factors.name: date_inconsistency
factors.description: Inconsistency between timestamps across sections: none, trivial (UTC vs local hour offset), or material (repair completed or surface laid before excavation opened, or inspection dated before surfacing)

sections.name: job
sections.description: Job reference, main ID, report and attendance timestamps, planned interruption estimate, nearby street works permits list

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Main material, nominal diameter, outside diameter in mm, install year, burst history list, replacement programme entry

sections.name: findings
sections.description: Excavation opened timestamp, depth, fracture type code, strike marks code, wall pitting grade, soil and ground movement readings

sections.name: repair
sections.description: Fitting type, fitting size range, fitting material, substitution reference, completion timestamp, pressure tests list

sections.name: network_ops
sections.description: Valve operations list with shut and open times, properties affected, rezoning flag, flushing log, water quality samples list

sections.name: reinstatement
sections.description: Surface layers list with type and laid date, highways inspection list with date and result

rendering_notes: fitting_size_mismatch: asset.od_mm (number) versus repair.fitting_range_mm {min,max}; trivial_rounding shows the range given in inches in repair.fitting_range_in alongside a near-boundary mm value inside tolerance; major puts asset.od_mm outside the range. substitution_approved: repair.substitution_ref string plus approver_code when true, null when false; it appears with and without mismatches about equally. pressure_test_outcome: repair.pressure_tests list of {test_at, test_bar, held_mins, result}; not_logged is an empty list. water_quality_state: network_ops.samples list of {taken_at, cl_residual_mgl, bact_result} where bact_result is 'pass', 'fail' or null for pending; flushing appears as network_ops.flushing list of {start, end}; low residual is below 0.2 mg/l. interruption_hours: derived only from network_ops.valve_ops list of {valve_id, op:'shut'|'open', at, customer_side:boolean}; the reviewer must take the earliest customer-side shut and latest customer-side open; network_ops.rezoned true with no customer-side valves means zero interruption; network_ops.properties_affected is a count and never a duration. estimate_drift: job.planned_interruption_mins is a decoy that may sit on the other side of 3 h or 12 h from the real duration. reinstatement_state: reinstatement.layers list of {layer:'temp_bitmac'|'base'|'wearing_course', laid_on} and reinstatement.inspections list of {on, result}; open means an empty layers list with job.barriers_in_place true; there is no stage or status field. failure_cause and strike_marks_ambiguous: findings.fracture_type ('puncture','circumferential','longitudinal','joint_pullout','pitting_hole'), findings.strike_marks ('yes','no','possible'), findings.wall_pitting_grade 0-4, findings.ground_movement_mm; there is no cause field. third_party_permit_timing: job.nearby_permits list of {permit_ref, works_type, start_on, distance_m}, compared with job.reported_at; after_report permits are decoys. prior_bursts_5y and prior_external_share: asset.burst_history list of {on, cause_code}, including some entries older than five years as decoys. replacement_scheduled: asset.replacement_programme {scheme_ref, planned_year} or null. date_inconsistency: findings.excavated_at, repair.completed_at, reinstatement layer and inspection dates; trivial cases show a one-hour offset with a 'Z' suffix on one field only. Records never contain fields such as cause, risk, priority, recommendation, close_out_status, interruption_band or reinstatement_stage; every answer must be inferred by comparing sections. Unknown values are null, not omitted. No free-text fields are present.
